title: Impact of Dividend Initiation on Stock Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Event Study
- Why: We observe daily stock returns around a clearly defined, firm-specific information event (dividend initiation announcement). Event studies estimate abnormal returns (AR) relative to a benchmark model and cumulate them over an event window to measure the market reaction.
- Implementation:
  - Compute abnormal returns using a risk-adjusted benchmark: AR = ret − beta × mkt_ret (CAPM-adjusted without alpha). This is the main specification given beta is provided.
  - Average across firms at day 0 to obtain the average abnormal return (AAR0) and test whether it is negative.
  - Compute mean CAR over short windows (e.g., [-1,+1], [0,+1]) as robustness.
  - Robustness: market-adjusted model (ret − mkt_ret), and market-model estimated on pre-event days (alpha, beta from days ≤ −1).
- Key assumptions:
  - No confounding firm-specific news tightly clustered with the announcement (no event contamination).
  - The expected return model is correctly specified locally (beta is stable over the short window; market is the main priced factor for our adjustment).
  - No systematic information leakage (or it is captured in pre-event returns); markets are semi-strong efficient so price reacts upon announcement.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required packages (base R is sufficient; stats is included by default)
# Complete, self-contained R code

# 1) Read data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s53_data.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Basic checks/cleaning
df <- df[is.finite(df$ret) & is.finite(df$mkt_ret) & is.finite(df$beta), ]
df <- df[order(df$stock_id, df$event_day), ]

# 2) Define abnormal return measures
# Main (CAPM-adjusted without alpha, using provided beta)
df$AR_capm <- df$ret - df$beta * df$mkt_ret

# Alternative 1: Market-adjusted (beta = 1, alpha = 0)
df$AR_ma <- df$ret - df$mkt_ret

# Alternative 2: Market model (alpha and beta estimated using pre-event data: event_day <= -1)
estimate_market_model <- function(d) {
  # Returns named vector c(alpha_hat, beta_hat)
  if (nrow(d) >= 5 && var(d$mkt_ret, na.rm = TRUE) > 0) {
    fit <- lm(ret ~ mkt_ret, data = d)
    coefs <- coef(fit)
    a <- ifelse(is.na(coefs[1]), 0, coefs[1])
    b <- ifelse(is.na(coefs[2]), 0, coefs[2])
    return(c(alpha_hat = a, beta_hat = b))
  } else {
    # Fallback: use alpha=0 and provided beta (median across days for that stock)
    b <- median(d$beta, na.rm = TRUE)
    return(c(alpha_hat = 0, beta_hat = b))
  }
}

pre_event <- df[df$event_day <= -1, ]
stocks <- sort(unique(df$stock_id))
mm_params <- do.call(rbind, lapply(stocks, function(s) {
  dpre <- pre_event[pre_event$stock_id == s, c("ret", "mkt_ret", "beta")]
  est <- estimate_market_model(dpre)
  data.frame(stock_id = s, alpha_hat = est["alpha_hat"], beta_hat = est["beta_hat"])
}))
df_mm <- merge(df, mm_params, by = "stock_id", all.x = TRUE)
df_mm$AR_mm <- with(df_mm, ret - (alpha_hat + beta_hat * mkt_ret))

# 3) Helper functions for event study stats
tstats_of_mean <- function(x, alternative = c("two.sided","less","greater")) {
  alternative <- match.arg(alternative)
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  n <- length(x)
  m <- mean(x)
  s <- sd(x)
  if (n < 2 || s == 0) {
    return(list(mean = m, n = n, t = NA_real_, p = NA_real_))
  }
  tval <- m / (s / sqrt(n))
  if (alternative == "two.sided") {
    p <- 2 * pt(abs(tval), df = n - 1, lower.tail = FALSE)
  } else if (alternative == "less") {
    p <- pt(tval, df = n - 1, lower.tail = TRUE)
  } else {
    p <- pt(tval, df = n - 1, lower.tail = FALSE)
  }
  list(mean = m, n = n, t = tval, p = p)
}

car_test <- function(dat, ar_col, w_start, w_end, require_complete = TRUE) {
  # dat must include: stock_id, event_day, and ar_col
  dd <- dat[dat$event_day >= w_start & dat$event_day <= w_end, c("stock_id","event_day", ar_col)]
  names(dd)[3] <- "AR"
  days <- seq(w_start, w_end, by = 1)
  car_vec <- sapply(unique(dd$stock_id), function(s) {
    tmp <- dd[dd$stock_id == s, ]
    have_days <- sort(unique(tmp$event_day))
    if (require_complete && length(intersect(have_days, days)) != length(days)) return(NA_real_)
    sum(tmp$AR[tmp$event_day %in% days], na.rm = TRUE)
  })
  car_vec <- car_vec[is.finite(car_vec)]
  # Two-sided and one-sided (less) tests
  two <- tstats_of_mean(car_vec, "two.sided")
  one_less <- tstats_of_mean(car_vec, "less")
  list(
    mean = two$mean,
    n = two$n,
    t = two$t,
    p_two_sided = two$p,
    p_one_sided_less = one_less$p
  )
}

winsorize <- function(x, probs = c(0.01, 0.99)) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  if (length(x) == 0) return(x)
  q <- quantile(x, probs = probs, na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE, type = 7)
  pmin(pmax(x, q[1]), q[2])
}

# 4) Main results: Announcement-day AAR and CARs (CAPM-adjusted)
aar0_capm <- with(df[df$event_day == 0, ], tstats_of_mean(AR_capm, alternative = "less"))  # H0: mean >= 0 vs H1: mean < 0
car_0_0_capm <- car_test(df[, c("stock_id","event_day","AR_capm")], "AR_capm", 0, 0, require_complete = TRUE)
car_m1_p1_capm <- car_test(df[, c("stock_id","event_day","AR_capm")], "AR_capm", -1, 1, require_complete = TRUE)
car_0_p1_capm <- car_test(df[, c("stock_id","event_day","AR_capm")], "AR_capm", 0, 1, require_complete = TRUE)

# 5) Robustness 1: Market-adjusted abnormal returns
aar0_ma <- with(df[df$event_day == 0, ], tstats_of_mean(AR_ma, alternative = "less"))
car_m1_p1_ma <- car_test(df[, c("stock_id","event_day","AR_ma")], "AR_ma", -1, 1, require_complete = TRUE)

# 6) Robustness 2: Market model (alpha, beta estimated on pre-event)
aar0_mm <- with(df_mm[df_mm$event_day == 0, ], tstats_of_mean(AR_mm, alternative = "less"))
car_m1_p1_mm <- car_test(df_mm[, c("stock_id","event_day","AR_mm")], "AR_mm", -1, 1, require_complete = TRUE)

# 7) Robustness 3: Winsorized CAPM AAR at day 0 (1% tails)
x0_capm <- df[df$event_day == 0, "AR_capm"]
x0_w <- winsorize(x0_capm, probs = c(0.01, 0.99))
# Recompute t-stats on winsorized sample (retain same N as original by trimming values, not observations)
# Align lengths by replacing extreme values in original vector
replace_wins <- function(orig, wins) {
  # Map winsorized values back to original order
  o <- orig[is.finite(orig)]
  # Determine cut points
  q <- quantile(o, probs = c(0.01, 0.99), na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE)
  o2 <- pmin(pmax(o, q[1]), q[2])
  o2
}
aar0_capm_wins <- tstats_of_mean(replace_wins(x0_capm, x0_w), alternative = "less")

# 8) Print clear numerical results
cat("Event Study: Dividend Initiation Announcement\n")
cat("--------------------------------------------------\n")
cat(sprintf("Number of unique stocks: %d\n", length(unique(df$stock_id))))
cat("Main result (CAPM-adjusted abnormal returns):\n")
cat(sprintf("  AAR on day 0 = %.4f (%.2f%%); t = %.2f; p(one-sided H<0) = %.4f; N = %d\n",
            aar0_capm$mean, 100*aar0_capm$mean, aar0_capm$t, aar0_capm$p, aar0_capm$n))
cat(sprintf("  CAR[0,0] (same as AAR0): mean = %.4f; t = %.2f; p(two-sided) = %.4f; N = %d\n",
            car_0_0_capm$mean, car_0_0_capm$t, car_0_0_capm$p_two_sided, car_0_0_capm$n))
cat(sprintf("  CAR[-1,+1]: mean = %.4f; t = %.2f; p(two-sided) = %.4f; N = %d\n",
            car_m1_p1_capm$mean, car_m1_p1_capm$t, car_m1_p1_capm$p_two_sided, car_m1_p1_capm$n))
cat(sprintf("  CAR[0,+1]: mean = %.4f; t = %.2f; p(two-sided) = %.4f; N = %d\n",
            car_0_p1_capm$mean, car_0_p1_capm$t, car_0_p1_capm$p_two_sided, car_0_p1_capm$n))

cat("\nRobustness checks:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Market-adjusted AAR0: mean = %.4f; t = %.2f; p(one-sided H<0) = %.4f; N = %d\n",
            aar0_ma$mean, aar0_ma$t, aar0_ma$p, aar0_ma$n))
cat(sprintf("  Market-adjusted CAR[-1,+1]: mean = %.4f; t = %.2f; p(two-sided) = %.4f; N = %d\n",
            car_m1_p1_ma$mean, car_m1_p1_ma$t, car_m1_p1_ma$p_two_sided, car_m1_p1_ma$n))
cat(sprintf("  Market-model (pre-event alpha,beta) AAR0: mean = %.4f; t = %.2f; p(one-sided H<0) = %.4f; N = %d\n",
            aar0_mm$mean, aar0_mm$t, aar0_mm$p, aar0_mm$n))
cat(sprintf("  Market-model CAR[-1,+1]: mean = %.4f; t = %.2f; p(two-sided) = %.4f; N = %d\n",
            car_m1_p1_mm$mean, car_m1_p1_mm$t, car_m1_p1_mm$p_two_sided, car_m1_p1_mm$n))
cat(sprintf("  Winsorized (1%% tails) CAPM AAR0: mean = %.4f; t = %.2f; p(one-sided H<0) = %.4f; N = %d\n",
            aar0_capm_wins$mean, aar0_capm_wins$t, aar0_capm_wins$p, aar0_capm_wins$n))

cat("\nInterpretation guide:\n")
cat("  - The key question is whether AAR0 < 0. Focus on p(one-sided H<0).\n")
cat("  - CAR over short windows should align in sign with AAR0 if the reaction is concentrated around day 0.\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive on the announcement day. Dividend initiations typically signal stronger, more predictable cash flows and managerial confidence, prompting a positive price reaction.
- Magnitude: AAR0 around +0.5% to +2.0% on average, with CAR[-1,+1] often in the +1% to +3% range. Given the small sample (≈100 firm-days total), statistical power is limited; significance may hinge on cross-sectional dispersion and the exact window coverage. Robustness specifications should yield consistent positive signs.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare CAR on announcement day to pre-announcement days.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Dividend initiation announcements lead to a negative CAR on the announcement day.
